goldenPoints: Oil-drop sign is the pathognomonic nail finding of psoriasis; Auspitz sign = pinpoint bleeding when scale is removed
Lichen planus = pruritic, purple, polygonal, flat-topped papules with Wickham striae on the flexor wrists
Leprosy reactions: Type 1 = Type IV hypersensitivity (borderline cases); Type 2 ENL = Type III (lepromatous side)
Erythrasma fluoresces coral-red under Wood's lamp
Scabies: burrows in the finger webs with itching worst at night — treat the whole body and all contacts
Secondary syphilis involves palms and soles; benzathine penicillin is the treatment
Basal cell carcinoma: pearly nodule, rolled beaded margin, peripheral palisading — and it almost never metastasises
Severe nodulocystic acne → oral isotretinoin (teratogenic — never in pregnancy)
In pregnancy, genital warts are treated with cryotherapy or TCA — podophyllin is contraindicated
A scar confined to the wound is a hypertrophic scar; one that outgrows it is a keloid
intro: Dermatology carries 5 questions per FMGE paper and is the most image-driven subject in the exam: stems describe a lesion in words and expect the diagnosis from morphology alone. Master the vocabulary of lesions, the classic sign attached to each common disease, and the one-line treatment of choice — that trio answers most stems.
subject: Dermatology
tagline: FMGE dermatology is image-based: morphology words, named signs and one-line treatments decide the answer

topics.askedAs: identify the test or lesion term
topics.oneLiner: Tzanck = herpes giant cells; Wood's lamp coral-red = erythrasma; a solid raised lesion under 0.5 cm is a papule.
points: Primary lesions: macule (flat colour change), papule (solid, <0.5 cm), plaque (flat-topped, >0.5 cm), nodule (solid, deeper, >0.5 cm)
Fluid lesions: vesicle (<0.5 cm), bulla (>0.5 cm), pustule (pus-filled); a wheal is a transient oedematous papule of urticaria
Secondary lesions: scale, crust, erosion (superficial, heals without scar), ulcer (deeper, scars), fissure, lichenification (thickened skin with exaggerated markings from rubbing)
Tzanck smear in herpes simplex/zoster shows multinucleated giant cells
Wood's lamp: erythrasma fluoresces coral-red; some tinea capitis fluoresces green; vitiligo is accentuated
KOH mount of scale or hair demonstrates fungal hyphae in dermatophyte infections
Nikolsky sign (skin shears off with gentle rubbing) is positive in pemphigus vulgaris and toxic epidermal necrolysis
Patch testing identifies allergic contact dermatitis — a Type IV hypersensitivity
Diascopy: a lesion that blanches under a glass slide is vascular; purpura does not blanch
topics.title: Skin Basics: Lesion Vocabulary & Bedside Tests
topics.trap: An erosion heals WITHOUT a scar but an ulcer scars — depth is the difference the exam is testing.

topics.askedAs: diagnosis from scale + sites; nail sign named
topics.oneLiner: Silvery scale on extensors + nail pitting + oil-drop sign = psoriasis, every time.
points: Chronic plaque psoriasis: well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery-white micaceous scales on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, scalp, sacrum)
Auspitz sign: removing the scale produces pinpoint bleeding points
Grattage test: scraping accentuates the scale before Auspitz bleeding appears
Nail changes: pitting, onycholysis, subungual hyperkeratosis — and the oil-drop (salmon patch) sign, considered pathognomonic
Koebner (isomorphic) phenomenon: new lesions appear at sites of trauma — seen in psoriasis, lichen planus and vitiligo
Guttate psoriasis: small drop-like lesions in a young patient after streptococcal sore throat
Histology: parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses in the stratum corneum, regular acanthosis and loss of the granular layer
Psoriatic arthritis affects the distal interphalangeal joints, with 'pencil-in-cup' deformity and sausage digits (dactylitis)
Treatment ladder: topical steroids and vitamin D analogues (calcipotriol) → phototherapy → methotrexate → biologics for severe disease
topics.title: Psoriasis & the Papulosquamous Group
topics.trap: Punctate nail pitting alone is not specific — the OIL-DROP sign is the one called pathognomonic for psoriasis.

topics.oneLiner: Purple polygonal papules + white lace (Wickham) + flexor wrists = lichen planus.
points: Lichen planus is summed up by the Ps: pruritic, purple, polygonal, plane (flat-topped) papules — classically on the flexor wrists, forearms and lower back
Wickham striae: fine white lacy lines on the surface of the papules
Lesions Koebnerise, so they often appear in linear arrays along scratch marks
Oral lichen planus gives lacy white (reticulate) lesions on the buccal mucosa that do not scrape off
Nail involvement causes longitudinal ridging, thinning and pterygium — the proximal nail fold grows forward over the nail bed
Lichen planus is associated with hepatitis C infection
Hypertrophic lichen planus occurs on the shins; lichen planopilaris causes scarring alopecia of the scalp
Treatment: potent topical corticosteroids for skin lesions; the condition often settles over 1–2 years
topics.title: Lichen Planus
topics.trap: Oral white lace that scrapes off is candidiasis; lichen planus Wickham striae do NOT scrape off.

topics.oneLiner: One anaesthetic patch = tuberculoid end; many symmetric lesions + leonine facies = lepromatous; Type 1 reaction is Type IV.
points: Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae; the slit-skin smear demonstrates acid-fast bacilli
Ridley–Jopling spectrum runs TT – BT – BB – BL – LL, from strong (TT) to absent (LL) cell-mediated immunity
Tuberculoid end: one or few well-defined, anaesthetic, hairless patches with early nerve damage
Lepromotous end: many symmetric lesions, nodules, leonine facies and madarosis (loss of eyebrows); sensation is lost late
WHO classification for treatment: paucibacillary = up to 5 skin lesions; multibacillary = more than 5 lesions
Nerves commonly thickened: ulnar (commonest), great auricular, common peroneal (lateral popliteal) and posterior tibial
Loss of sensation over the back of the ear points to the great auricular nerve
Type 1 (reversal) reaction: a Type IV hypersensitivity in borderline leprosy — existing lesions inflame and acute neuritis threatens nerve function
Type 2 reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum): a Type III hypersensitivity on the lepromatous side — crops of tender red nodules with fever
Multidrug therapy combines rifampicin, dapsone and clofazimine; clofazimine itself causes reddish-brown skin pigmentation
Deformities to know: claw hand (ulnar), foot drop (common peroneal), lagophthalmos (facial), saddle nose (lepromatous)
topics.title: Leprosy
topics.trap: Type 1 reaction is Type IV (cell-mediated) and Type 2 ENL is Type III (immune-complex) — FMGE swaps them deliberately.

topics.askedAs: organism or diagnosis from itch/site history
topics.oneLiner: Night itch + finger-web burrows = scabies; nodules climbing a limb after a thorn prick = sporotrichosis.
points: Scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei): intense itching worst at night, burrows in finger webs, wrists, axillae and genitals; close contacts are usually affected too
Scabies treatment: permethrin 5% cream applied to the whole body, repeated as advised, with simultaneous treatment of all contacts and hot washing of linen
Impetigo: honey-coloured crusted lesions, from Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
Erysipelas is a superficial, sharply demarcated, bright-red cellulitis, classically on the face; cellulitis is deeper and less demarcated
Herpes zoster: grouped vesicles in a dermatome with burning pain — in an elderly patient, oral acyclovir/valacyclovir started early is the appropriate treatment
Molluscum contagiosum: pearly papules with central umbilication, caused by a poxvirus
Sporotrichosis follows a thorn prick in farmers and gardeners: a nodule at the site, then further nodules ascending along the lymphatics
Mycetoma: a swollen foot with multiple discharging sinuses that extrude grains
Erythrasma is a bacterial (Corynebacterium) infection of the flexures, not a fungus — hence its coral-red Wood's lamp fluorescence
topics.title: Skin Infections & Infestations
topics.trap: Erythrasma looks like a fungal flexural rash but is bacterial — the coral-red fluorescence is the giveaway.

topics.oneLiner: Painless hard chancre = syphilis; painful soft ulcer = chancroid; painless beefy-red = donovanosis.
points: Primary syphilis: a single painless, indurated (hard) chancre with painless regional nodes
Secondary syphilis: a generalised rash that characteristically involves the palms and soles, condyloma lata in moist folds, moth-eaten alopecia and epitrochlear lymphadenopathy
Benzathine penicillin is the treatment of choice for syphilis
Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi): painful, soft genital ulcers with a tender inguinal bubo
Donovanosis (granuloma inguinale): a painless, beefy-red, granular ulcer that bleeds easily, without significant lymphadenopathy
Lymphogranuloma venereum: a fleeting painless ulcer followed by painful buboes that may straddle the inguinal ligament (groove sign)
Genital herpes: painful grouped vesicles that recur at the same site
Genital warts (HPV 6 and 11): podophyllin/podophyllotoxin is contraindicated in pregnancy — cryotherapy or trichloroacetic acid is the treatment of choice
topics.title: Sexually Transmitted Skin Disease
topics.trap: In a pregnant woman with genital warts, the 'usual' answer podophyllin is teratogenic/unsafe — pregnancy changes the treatment of choice to cryotherapy.

topics.askedAs: antibody or sign matched to disease
topics.oneLiner: Anti-Scl-70 = diffuse scleroderma; heliotrope + Gottron = dermatomyositis; brick-wall skin = Hailey–Hailey.
points: Diffuse systemic sclerosis: tight, shiny, thickened skin with sclerodactyly and Raynaud phenomenon; antibody is anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70)
Limited systemic sclerosis (CREST) is linked to the anti-centromere antibody
Dermatomyositis: heliotrope (violaceous) eyelid rash and Gottron papules over the knuckles, with proximal muscle weakness — difficulty climbing stairs or combing hair
Dermatomyositis in adults is associated with internal malignancy
Cutaneous sarcoidosis: non-caseating granulomas, with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum and lupus pernio
Hailey–Hailey disease (familial benign chronic pemphigus) shows the 'dilapidated brick wall' appearance on histopathology
Pemphigus vulgaris: flaccid bullae, positive Nikolsky sign and oral erosions; fish-net intercellular IgG on immunofluorescence
Bullous pemphigoid: tense bullae in the elderly, Nikolsky negative
Erythema nodosum (tender shin nodules) is associated with sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, streptococcal infection, drugs and inflammatory bowel disease
topics.title: Autoimmune & Connective-Tissue Skin Disease
topics.trap: Pemphigus bullae are FLACCID (roof is thin, intraepidermal) while pemphigoid bullae are TENSE (subepidermal) — the stem usually hands you this word.

topics.askedAs: hair loss pattern or acne severity treatment
topics.oneLiner: Chemotherapy sheds growing hair = anagen effluvium; stress sheds resting hair months later = telogen effluvium.
points: Acne vulgaris: comedones are the hallmark lesion; the organism implicated is Cutibacterium (Propionibacterium) acnes
Acne treatment ladder: topical retinoid/benzoyl peroxide for mild disease, add antibiotics for inflammatory disease
Severe nodulocystic or scarring acne: oral isotretinoin is the treatment of choice — it is teratogenic and needs strict pregnancy avoidance
Corticosteroids are NOT a treatment for acne — they can themselves cause acneiform eruptions
Acne fulminans is an explosive, ulcerative acne with systemic upset (fever, joint pains)
Androgenetic alopecia: patterned hair loss (frontotemporal recession and vertex thinning in men) driven by dihydrotestosterone
Alopecia areata: patchy non-scarring hair loss with exclamation-mark hairs at the margins
Telogen effluvium: diffuse shedding 2–3 months after childbirth, fever, surgery or severe stress
Anagen effluvium: abrupt loss of growing hairs, classically from chemotherapy
Trichotillomania: hair pulling producing patches with broken hairs of many different lengths and no scaling
topics.title: Acne, Hair & Nail Disorders
topics.trap: Isotretinoin is the answer for severe acne — unless the patient is pregnant, when it becomes the most dangerous option.

topics.oneLiner: Pearly rolled margin + palisading = BCC; follicular hyperkeratosis (toad skin) = vitamin A deficiency.
points: Basal cell carcinoma: a pearly papule/nodule with a rolled, beaded margin and surface telangiectasia, classically near the medial canthus; it ulcerates as a 'rodent ulcer'
BCC histology shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading; metastasis is exceedingly rare
Squamous cell carcinoma grows faster, can metastasise, and can arise in a chronic burn scar (Marjolin ulcer)
Malignant melanoma: suspect any mole changing in Asymmetry, Border, Colour, Diameter or Evolution (ABCDE)
Kaposi sarcoma: violaceous plaques and nodules, associated with HHV-8 and HIV
Vitiligo: acquired depigmented macules, autoimmune, Koebner-positive, accentuated under Wood's lamp, associated with autoimmune thyroid disease
Melasma: symmetric brown facial pigmentation worsened by sun exposure and hormonal factors (pregnancy, oral contraceptives)
Phrynoderma — follicular hyperkeratosis ('toad skin') — is the classic cutaneous sign of vitamin A deficiency
Zinc deficiency causes delayed wound healing, alopecia and periorificial dermatitis (acrodermatitis enteropathica)
A hypertrophic scar stays WITHIN the original wound margins and may regress; a keloid grows BEYOND them
Infantile (strawberry) haemangioma grows in the first months then involutes spontaneously over years — uncomplicated lesions need observation and reassurance
topics.title: Skin Tumours, Pigmentation & Deficiency Signs
topics.trap: Scar confined to the incision = hypertrophic scar, not keloid — keloid by definition outgrows the wound.
